resets.asserted_meaning: Immediately sets the state register to S0 on the rising assertion of reset; the output then reflects S0.

ports.name: in
ports.role: Serial input bit; the RTL samples its conditional-operator result into next_state before the active clock edge.

ports.name: reset
ports.role: Active-high asynchronous reset to state S0.

ports.name: out
ports.role: Moore output: high while the state is S4 after recognizing input pattern 1101.

declared_unknowns.description: present_state, next_state, and out have no declaration-time initialization. Before reset establishes S0, their observable result can remain X; the testbench checks the initial X output.

The RTL case statement has no default arm. For invalid or unknown present_state encodings, next_state and out retain their previous values; this latch behavior is preserved. A directed X input test checks transition to an invalid state and asynchronous reset recovery.
Directed X tests cover the input conditional merge and a 0-to-X reset event (including the RTL procedural-if else branch). Z on data/reset and X/Z clock transitions are not separately tested.
RTL parameters S0..S4 use defaults 0..4. The SystemC module models these defaults; parameter overrides are not exposed or verified.

The S4 transition on input 1 goes to S1 and treats that subsequent bit as the start of a new match. The RTL permits adjacent nonoverlapping 1101 detections (for example 11011101); this literal transition behavior is retained.
